about: Local government in England under the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026: what is in force, and what is planned. Transcribed by hand from the primary sources linked on each fact, read on 22 November 2026. Secondary sources are used only where marked secondary, and only for a summary of the Act. Nothing here is inferred: a status the sources don't give is left out.

tiers.label: Single foundation strategic authority
tiers.plain: One county council or unitary council given strategic powers on its own.
tiers.law: A unitary district council or county council designated under section 3.

tiers.label: Combined foundation strategic authority
tiers.plain: Several councils working together as a combined authority, without a mayor.
tiers.law: A non-mayoral combined authority or combined county authority.

tiers.label: Mayoral strategic authority
tiers.plain: A group of councils with an elected mayor, who has more powers and money.
tiers.law: A mayoral combined authority, a mayoral combined county authority, or the Greater London Authority.

tiers.label: Established mayoral strategic authority
tiers.plain: A mayoral authority with a strong track record, given the most powers and a single funding settlement.
tiers.law: A mayoral strategic authority that has been designated as established.

value: Health, well-being and public service reform

changes.now: Mayors and police and crime commissioners are elected by the supplementary vote again: voters mark a first and a second choice. The May 2026 mayoral elections still used first past the post.
A mayor of a strategic authority can't also be a member of a UK legislature.
Councils can no longer choose the committee system of running a council. Most councils already use a leader and cabinet; a council with a 'protected' committee system may keep it but must review it.

summary.value: England's two-tier areas (a county council with district councils under it) are being replaced by single-tier unitary councils. There are 21 areas. Surrey's two new councils start on 1 April 2027. Five areas have 'minded to' decisions (29 October 2026). The other 15 are under review after decisions were withdrawn in September and October 2026; every area is due an outcome by early 2027.

postponed_2026.value: Of 136 council elections due in May 2026, 29 were postponed to help reorganisation; 107 went ahead.

minded-to.label: Minded to go ahead
minded-to.plain: The government intends to go ahead and is hearing final views before it decides.

review.label: Under review
review.plain: An earlier decision was withdrawn, or none was made. All options are still open.
